title: Closed immersions of algebraic spaces are proper
statement: Algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space], schemes use [def-pc-scheme], and universes use [def-weil-size-convention]. Their point spaces have the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]; fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, quasi-compact, locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and universally closed. Separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion; universally closed means closed on point spaces after every algebraic-space base change [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A closed immersion of algebraic spaces means a representable morphism whose every scheme base change is a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $S$ be a scheme and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of algebraic spaces over $S$. Then $i$ is proper. No finite-presentation, Noetherian, reducedness, or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $S$-scheme $T$ and map $h_T\to X$. The hypothesis that $i$ is a closed immersion supplies a scheme $Z_T$ representing $Z\times_Xh_T$ and a closed immersion $i_T:Z_T\to T$ of schemes; this is precisely the quantified scheme-test condition in the definition of a closed immersion given in the statement. Apply clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] to $i_T$. It is a proper scheme morphism. Since $T\to X$ was arbitrary, every represented scheme pullback of $i$ is proper. No finite-presentation assumption on its defining ideal is used.

source.place: Tag 04XZ (lemma-closed-immersion-proper), applying scheme Tag 01W5 (lemma-closed-immersion-proper) on each test; the universal-quantifier argument is the specialization of spaces.tex Tag 02YO (lemma-representable-transformations-property-implication).

proof.text: The closed-immersion hypothesis also supplies representability of $i$ by schemes. Thus the reverse direction of [lem-sfb-space-representable-proper-tests] applies to $i:Z\to X$ and to the family of proper scheme projections established in step 1. It gives intrinsic properness of $i$: separatedness, quasi-compactness, local finite type on etale charts and closedness on points after every algebraic-space base change, exactly as required. The criterion supplies the passage from scheme tests to arbitrary algebraic-space base changes; we do not identify that passage with a definition.
